note:
Decisive evidence for this bug from #2578's Step 9c gate (2026-08-25), independently reproduced from on-disk artifacts by two agents.

The contradiction is INTERNAL to the workflow surface and pins the fix location precisely:

- `parse_junit_failure_texts` (scripts/step9c_baseline.py:1327) DOCUMENTS its input contract in its own docstring, line 1335: "both carry the full accumulated violation list under the gate's `--tb=no` xunit1 flags — #2316 plan A1 probe".
- The canonical gate launcher emitted by `select_step9c_tests.py --emit-launcher` runs `-v --tb=short`.
- `PYTEST_BASE_FLAGS` (line 473) gives the PRISTINE side `-q --tb=no`.

So the parser's documented precondition and the launcher's emitted flags disagree, and the pristine side silently satisfies the precondition while the branch side violates it. That asymmetry is the whole bug.

Mechanism, reproduced: `_VIOLATION_ROW_RE` (line 392) is `^[ \t]*(?:E[ \t]+)?(?:[-*][ \t]+)?((?:scripts|src|tests|configs|docs)/[\w./-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)` — `tests` is in the path alternation and the match is anchored at line start. A `--tb=short` traceback location line therefore matches. Parsing #2578's real gate junit with `parse_junit_failure_texts` showed EXACTLY ONE row contributing the phantom token: `tests/test_shared_vm_thread_caps.py:1000: in test_no_new_torch_before_dotenv_vm_entrypoints`.

Result on #2578: compare reported `new_violations: ["tests/test_shared_vm_thread_caps.py"]` — the test file itself — for `tests/test_shared_vm_thread_caps.py::test_no_new_torch_before_dotenv_vm_entrypoints`, while the four genuine offenders were identical on both sides and byte-identical to base. The round's payload has zero torch imports and the worktree had zero untracked files, so no legitimate route to that violation existed. Cost: a mechanically-correct FAIL verdict on a clean round, plus a verification round to establish it.

Two candidate fixes, and the docstring says which is intended: (a) make the parser tolerant of `--tb=short` by dropping traceback location rows (a location row is `<path>:<lineno>: in <name>` / `<path>:<lineno>: <ExcType>` — distinguishable from a violation row by the trailing `:<int>:`), or (b) make the gate launcher emit `--tb=no` so the documented precondition holds. (a) preserves gate diagnosability; (b) matches the docstring's stated assumption but costs human-readable tracebacks in the gate log.

Note for whoever takes this: the blast radius is every Step 9c gate whenever ANY `VIOLATION_SET_SCAN_NODES` member is red on main, which is the current state of main — so this false-FAILs rounds fleet-wide, not just occasionally.

Minimal single-variable reproduction of this bug, from #2578. ~75 seconds to run; no gate needed.

Same node, same worktree, same parser, ONE variable changed:

  uv run pytest tests/test_shared_vm_thread_caps.py::test_no_new_torch_before_dotenv_vm_entrypoints \
    -q --tb=no    -p no:cacheprovider -o junit_family=xunit1 --junitxml=/tmp/probe-tbno.xml
  uv run pytest tests/test_shared_vm_thread_caps.py::test_no_new_torch_before_dotenv_vm_entrypoints \
    -q --tb=short -p no:cacheprovider -o junit_family=xunit1 --junitxml=/tmp/probe-tbshort.xml

Then parse BOTH with the production parser and the production regex (register the module in sys.modules BEFORE exec_module, or @dataclass resolution raises AttributeError on NoneType):

  texts = m.parse_junit_failure_texts(path)
  rows  = {mm.group(1) for line in txt.splitlines() if (mm := m._VIOLATION_ROW_RE.match(line))}

Result:

  --tb=no    -> 4 rows: scripts/issue1901_mlpdense_fold_analysis.py, scripts/issue1901_mlpdense_fold_figures.py, scripts/issue2254_firstk_ctxext_sensitivity.py, scripts/issue2378_lenmatch_fig.py
  --tb=short -> those same 4 PLUS tests/test_shared_vm_thread_caps.py
  set difference == exactly {tests/test_shared_vm_thread_caps.py}; nothing else moves.

So the phantom is fully attributable to the tb verbosity flag, and the injected token is the TEST FILE ITSELF — a path the test's own _scan_targets scope (tracked scripts/**/*.py plus __main__-guarded src/experiments modules) can never legitimately produce.

This doubles as a ready-made regression test for the fix: assert the parsed violation set is INVARIANT across --tb=no and --tb=short for a node whose failure message carries a violation list. A fix that only special-cases the ':<lineno>: in <name>' shape should also be checked against the ':<lineno>: <ExcType>' shape, which --tb=short emits for exception failures rather than assertion failures.

Empirical note on blast radius: with this asymmetry live, ANY branch whose gate run has a red VIOLATION_SET_SCAN_NODES member gets a false SCAN-NEW-VIOLATION, because the phantom is the test file — which is present on the branch side by construction and absent from the --tb=no pristine side by construction. It does not depend on what the branch changed.

DECISIVE confirmation by controlled experiment, from /issue 2578 Step 9c. This supersedes my earlier note on this task, which argued the artifact from converging circumstantial observations; this is the direct test.

## Design

Same branch, same 235-file gate set, same suite state. ONE variable changed: the gate's traceback flag, `--tb=short` -> `--tb=no`. `-o junit_family=xunit1` held untouched and re-asserted pre-launch; launcher verified to carry `--tb=no` and not `--tb=short` before it ran.

Held-constant check, not assumed: I extracted the failing-node set from both rounds' junit and diffed them. BYTE-IDENTICAL, 13 nodes, the same 13. So the flag altered nothing about which tests fail — only the failure TEXT that `parse_junit_failure_texts` consumes.

## Result

| | round 1 (`--tb=short`) | round 2 (`--tb=no`) |
|---|---|---|
| gate | 13 failed / 8777 passed | 13 failed / 8777 passed (same nodes) |
| compare rc | 1 | **0** |
| NEW | 1 | **0** |
| stripped | 12 | **13** |
| `new_violations` | `["tests/test_shared_vm_thread_caps.py"]` | **`[]`** |
| `pre_existing` | 4 files | **same 4 files, byte-identical** |

The phantom violation `tests/test_shared_vm_thread_caps.py` is present under `--tb=short` and absent under `--tb=no`, with the genuine `pre_existing` set unchanged across both. The node that classified NEW in round 1 now strips legitimately `via: pristine-scratch`.

## Mechanism, confirmed end to end

`parse_junit_failure_texts` (`step9c_baseline.py:1327`) declares its input contract in its own docstring at line 1335: "both carry the full accumulated violation list under the gate's `--tb=no` xunit1 flags". The canonical emitted launcher runs `--tb=short`, so the production gate feeds the parser input it does not claim to handle. `_VIOLATION_ROW_RE` (line 392) has `tests` in its path alternation, so it matches the traceback LOCATION line and injects the test file itself into the branch-side violation set. The pristine side runs `PYTEST_BASE_FLAGS` (line 473, `-q --tb=no`) and structurally cannot emit that line, so the diff reports a NEW violation that exists only in the branch's traceback verbosity.

Two independent grounds confirm the flagged path was never a real violation: the reported "violation" is the TEST FILE itself, and `tests/` is never in that test's own `_scan_targets` scope (tracked `scripts/**/*.py` plus `__main__`-guarded modules).

## Cost of the artifact in this one round

A false FAIL on a clean payload, ~2.5h of gate wall to re-run, ~1h of compare, plus three attempts at the compare leg. It also came close to producing a wrong conclusion: the mechanically-correct verdict was FAIL, and the only thing separating "instrument artifact" from "real defect I have not found" was reading the parser's docstring.

## Suggested fix shape

Either align the emitted launcher with the parser's declared contract (`--tb=no`), or make the parser robust to traceback location lines (anchor on the accumulated-violation-list block rather than any path-shaped row). The launcher change is a one-token fix and was sufficient here; the parser hardening is the durable one, since the docstring's precondition is otherwise enforced only by convention. Whichever ships, pin it — a test asserting the emitted launcher's tb flag matches what the parser documents.

Round-1 artifacts preserved at /tmp/issue-2578-round1-keep/ (junit + log at `--tb=short`) for anyone wanting to reproduce the parse directly against real input.
